label: lem:linear_decomp_unique
title: Uniqueness of linear sieve decomposition
statement:
Let $m$ be composite.
    Then there is at most one linear sieve decomposition $(a,p)$ of $m$.
proof: If $(a_1, p_1)$ and $(a_2, p_2)$ are both decompositions, then both $p_1$ and $p_2$ are the least prime factor of $m$, so $p_1 = p_2$. Then $a_1 = m/p_1 = m/p_2 = a_2$.
